content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to [product_name]. I'm running [product_name] [version_no] on Windows 7 Pro and want to import an existing ladder diagram (*.lld), but it seems only FBD diagrams (*.lsc) files are accepted for import. I've set Ladder as the default editor under tools > options > general. Is there a way to bypass this limitation or am I missing something?
For [product_name] [version_no], both LAD and FBD diagrams are available in diagram mode. However, network project mode restricts import and creation to FBD files only.
I want to import an existing ladder diagram into a new [product_name] [article_no] within the project tree. How can this be done?

This can't be done directly. In network project mode, only FBD (*.lsc) files can be imported. You'll need to open the *.lld file in regular diagram mode, use the 'Convert to FBD' button, save the created .lsc file, then import that. Once in network project mode, converting back to LAD isn't supported.

It seems there's some misunderstanding here—maybe even on my part. Could you provide a screenshot to clarify what you mean, please? Is there a particular reason you aren't opening the program by the usual method?

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience restrictions when importing ladder diagram (*.lld) files in [product_name] [version_no], particularly in network project mode, which only accepts FBD (*.lsc) files. The only way to work with ladder diagrams involves converting them to FBD within diagram mode, and returning to ladder format is not possible in network project mode. This exposes a workflow limitation that can be inconvenient for those accustomed to ladder diagrams.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to allow easy import and use of ladder diagram (*.lld) files in network project mode, or at least provide a simple method for working with existing ladder diagrams.
